title: queued-throttle-forensics-scratch-dominique
content:
Purpose: quick forensic scratchpad for an odd queued-throttle pattern observed on staging 2025-11-02. Goal: capture hypotheses, exact repro steps, metrics snapshot, and triage next actions before I forget.

Summary of the problem: intermittent, short-lived tail spikes (p99) with correlated queue growth in dispatcher queue despite low global GPU utilization (~22%). Spikes last 3–12s, appear when mixed-size requests (small system prompt completions + occasional long context scoring) arrive in close succession. Not steady — triggered by particular arrival ordering.

High-level hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: token-bucket refill + dispatcher batching alignment causes transient admission collapse: lots of small requests wait until a long request consumes batch slot -> queue forms -> short throttle.
- H2: KV-cache prefill for long-context requests causes temporary scheduling priority inversion (worker pinned while OOM/evicting) -> other tasks queue up behind it.
- H3: backend preemption/GC-like pause (python worker GC or CUDA context switch) for the node that picked the long request -> request inflight stalls and queues pile up at proxy.
- H4: rate-limiter per-tenant burst smoothing is misconfigured (window too coarse) so bursts that cross bucket boundary appear as sudden drops in admission.

Repro notes / minimal harness I ran (commands):
- generators: bench-client with arrival trace: "small=0.95,long=0.05" mixed Poisson arrivals + occasional 200ms microburst (script attached in GH PR but pasted below).
- bench-client flags: --qps 180 --concurrency 120 --pattern poisson-mix --payload-distribution small:short,long:10k-tokens
- server config snapshot: dispatcher.batch_max_tokens=4096, dispatcher.max_batch_time_ms=12, admission.token_bucket_capacity=200, refill_rate=100 qps, worker-eviction-threshold=0.78, kvcache-prefetch=true

Raw sample (timestamped) metrics during a 10m run (selected window):
- 00:03:12 - global QPS 184, in_flight 62, dispatcher_queue_len 14, gpu_util 21%, p50 28ms, p95 320ms, p99 6.1s
- 00:03:16 - spike start: QPS 188, in_flight 120 (concurrency cap hit), dispatcher_queue_len 87, gpu_util 19%, p50 26ms, p95 410ms, p99 7.9s
- 00:03:24 - spike end: QPS 175, in_flight 58, dispatcher_queue_len 3, gpu_util 22%, p99 82ms
Notes: when concurrency saturates we see dispatcher queue grow rapidly; many entries in trace show a long request occupying a worker for ~5–8s (matches p99).

Instrumentation I added (quick hacks):
- added per-request lifecycle markers (proxy->dispatcher->worker) with micro-times printed in trace.
- added a counter for "worker-blocked-on-prefetch" when KV prefetch is active.
- instrumented token-bucket state dumps every 500ms during runs (capacity, tokens, last_refill_ts).

Preliminary findings:
- token-bucket occasionally reports 0 tokens for 300–900ms following a short concentrated burst; refill semantics show refill happens in 100ms ticks (coarse), so admission is clumpy.
- long requests often show worker lifecycle: proxy(12ms) -> dispatcher(6ms) -> worker(start) -> kv-prefetch(120–360ms) -> model-inference(3.9–7.1s). While prefetch was happening, that worker marked as "busy" and did not accept coalesced small requests.
- GPU on affected machines does not show a corresponding jump in util during prefetch -> cost is CPU+I/O bound for prefetch.
- occasional CUDA stream sync (observed via perf counters) when long requests escalate from 4k->10k token decoding; this introduced 40–150ms jitter on the worker thread at specific seq breakpoints.

Quick conclusions:
- token-bucket + coarse refill + high concurrency creates a brittle admission surface; when refill misses align with a long worker that has prefetch overhead, admission collapses briefly and the dispatcher queue builds.
- KV prefetch cost (CPU blocking) is a substantial contributor; offloading prefetch or doing async prefetch could reduce hold time.
- worker-level backpressure (e.g., accept-only-if-free or soft-handshake) might help — avoid dedicating a worker to prefetch-only while small tasks pile up.

Actions / experiments to run next (prio ordered):
1) Lower dispatcher.max_batch_time_ms from 12 -> 6 ms to reduce batching waiting windows; measure effect on p95/p99 and throughput. (Low risk)
2) Change token-bucket refill granularity to 10ms vs current 100ms tick to smooth admission. (Medium risk, needs perf test)
3) Toggle kvcache-prefetch=false for the long requests; run the same mixed workload to see delta on p99. (Quick A/B)
4) Implement worker soft-accept: allow worker to accept prefetch tasks but immediately yield small request slot if small requests queue exceeds threshold. (Longer dev)
5) Add an admission policy experiment: prefer small-completion-first (SJF-ish) when queue contains >X small requests. (Explore)

Quick measurement plan for each experiment: keep the same arrival trace, run three 10m trials per variant, capture p50/p95/p99, dispatcher_queue_len histogram, in_flight over time, token-bucket dump samples. Use bench-client seed 20251103 to keep synthetic traffic identical.

Scratch log of the very first test (2025-11-03 09:42 local): changed only kvcache-prefetch=false for long requests. Observed: p99 reduced from ~6.8s -> ~1.2s in that 5m window, dispatcher_queue_len never >10. Throughput steady at 178 qps. Means prefetch is heavy contributor. Need to verify whether disabling prefetch increases model latency (it did increase model inference time by ~120ms average for long requests) but overall user-facing p99 much better.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does token-bucket hit zero for ~300–900ms under these mixes? Is burst smoothing algorithm tuned for uniform arrivals only?
- Is there an interaction with autoscaler or scheduler that temporarily reduces worker acceptance windows? (check kube pod CPU steal events)
- Does prefetch I/O contend with other housekeeping tasks (checkpointing, dumping telemetry) at exact same times? correlate with node-level iostat.

Notes-to-self: capture the bench-client trace files and upload to /tmp/bench-20251103 for sharing; push quick patch to flip kvcache-prefetch flag in serving-runtime config for A/B test and link PR. Add an e2e run in CI to ensure token-bucket change doesn't regress fairness for other tenants.

Immediate next steps (today):
- Run experiment #1 (batch_time_ms -> 6) - 3x10m runs, collect traces (Dominique).
- Push quick config change and run kv-pretech=false A/B repeat (Dominique + Aisha).
- Open short ticket to investigate token-bucket refill internals (assign Ravi).
- Post summary + annotated trace to #runtime-bench with the key snippet and link to PR.

References / pasted snippets:
- bench-client invocation (simplified):
  python bench/client.py --target https://staging.redwood/api/generate --pattern poisson-mix --qps 180 --concurrency 120 --seed 20251103 --payload-config payloads/mix-small-long.json

- quick token-bucket dump (sample):
  {ts: 1700002992.513, capacity: 200, tokens: 0, last_refill_delta_ms: 96}
  {ts: 1700002993.112, capacity: 200, tokens: 62, last_refill_delta_ms: 104}

- topology note: these runs targeted the small fleet pool (3 x A100s, cpu-heavy prefetch machine class).

If anyone grabs this: leave comments inline. I'll update after experiment #1.

-- Dominique
